title: World Happiness Report

definition.text: An annual publication that ranks national happiness from people's own ratings of their lives and correlates them with quality-of-life factors.

facts.text: Rankings rest on one life-evaluation question, the Cantril ladder, in which respondents rate their current life from 0 (worst) to 10 (best); the data come mainly from the Gallup World Poll.

The report grew out of UN General Assembly resolution 65/309 (2011), which invited countries to measure happiness to guide public policy; the first report appeared in April 2012 for a UN meeting on a new economic paradigm.

Six factors (such as GDP per capita and social support) are compared with a hypothetical nation, Dystopia, to explain scores, but they do not change a country's total; the variables show correlation, not causation.

Critics note evaluations differ from daily emotional experience (Colombia ranked 37th in 2018 yet first on Gallup's Positive Experience Index) and that a single-item measure differs from multi-indicator indexes such as the HDI.

contested_note: Whether single-item and multi-item scales best measure life satisfaction is still debated.

title: WELLBY

definition.text: A well-being-adjusted life-year, a unit the World Happiness Report supports for judging policy by changes in life satisfaction.

facts.text: Since 2021 the World Happiness Report has backed WELLBYs, contrasting them with QALYs, which count only a patient's health quality.
The report says policy-makers should aim to raise the WELLBYs of people alive today and of future generations.
